security_privacy_cost_impact: Tightens only. A settled approval request is frozen for every UPDATE, upsert or MERGE of a writer that fires triggers: its status, decided_by and decided_at, and since the review round every other column but updated_at and updated_by; an INSERT that names a decider is timed by the database. Probes added or hardened: the verdict ties each refusal to its object and its transaction; psql meta-commands, and the shapes on which psql could lex a source otherwise, are refused in every SQL source before anything runs; every trigger on approval_requests and the functions they run (body, owner) are pinned; a parameter grant of session_replication_role is refused; every non-superuser role's privileges on the two calendar tables, grant options included, are held to an allowlist under a superuser owner; no rewrite rule in app or private; nothing created in pg_catalog, checked in every probe job. No grant is added. No secret or customer data.
migration_and_data_impact: ONE MIGRATION: 126_approval_decision_frozen_for_every_writer.sql (replaces private.set_decided_at()'s body, recreates its trigger BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE, adds CHECK (decided_at >= created_at), apply-time block). 125's block superseded by a final-state replacement in db/foundation/invariants/. Declared in the snapshot's not-applied tail. The CHECK applies over no rows: no environment holds approval data before G0.
compatibility_impact: Additive and forward. Cases stay 1058; tests stay 675; the foundation-contract assertion floor 365 -> 418 (more assertions now, floor unchanged). Probes 12 -> 16. A writer that inserts a decided approval request no longer keeps the decided_at it sent (O3); no writer that fires triggers can move a request out of a non-pending state (O4) or change any column of a settled request but updated_at and updated_by. psqlLex now also refuses a bare CR, any mention of standard_conforming_strings and a quote after an odd run of backslashes in a plain literal; no current source carries one.
known_limitations: Blocker 186 (15)'s command-role half: the settled-row closure for an RFC-2026-023 command role waits on that RFC; and with it DELETE: a writer holding DELETE (today only the owner and a superuser) can delete a settled request and insert it again as anything (C0 F2, A1 F2). No BEFORE DELETE refusal is added: it would pre-empt (16)'s erasure route.

Blocker 186 (16), the anonymisation route batch 160 needs, which must now account for status and every other column of a settled request; (20), INFO, except the transaction-control check now running before the drifts.

A superuser still bypasses the trigger with session_replication_role or DISABLE TRIGGER (caught in a later file by the trigger probe); ALTER SYSTEM is not covered. A hostile superuser drift can still forge in ways no verdict sees; the pg_catalog guard covers functions, operators and casts, not a catalog row edited in place under allow_system_table_mods.
psqlLex is not psql's lexer: its claim is the shapes measured and the list in its comment. It over-refuses a SQL-standard `begin atomic ... end` body (fails closed; no drift uses one).

The grant allowlist covers the two calendar tables only; the general version over every RLS table in app is not attempted. C0 H1's optional case owner-a-cannot-place-an-item-already-deleted is not added. The rewrite rule probe covers app and private only.
